newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse in talks on new stock trading system.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse in talks on new stock trading system.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange said on Monday it had entered negotiations with a French and Australian supplier on a new computer system for trading in equities.

"The Oslo Stock Exchange has since the summer of 1996 been in contact with suppliers of a new equity trading system. The project is now in a negotiation phase with two suppliers; the French SBF -- Paris Bourse and the Australian Computershare Systems Limited (CSL)," a newsletter said.

"Final negotiations will be completed early this summer, whereby Phase 2 begins with implementations of the new equity trading system," it said. "The new system is scheduled to be in production by 1998."

The bourse originally had planned to have a new trading system in place in 1996, but in March last year it cancelled a 51 million crown contract with Logica Plc for the system because of alleged delays caused by the British software company.
The new electronic trading system will provide users with an automatch system, as opposed to the current system where orders are matched manually by phone.
Decentralised, off-floor trade will allow for overseas brokers to become members of the Oslo Bourse, one of the smallest in Europe.
"The new equity trading system will enable the brokers, regardless of location, to trade on the Oslo Stock Exchange in an efficient, fair and affordable way," the newsletter said.
To minimise risk and to provide a smooth transition in the implementation phase, the new equity trading system will be a proven system as it is currently being used by another exchange, it said.
The system will be delivered within 9 months after the contract is signed.

"As the introduction of a new equity trading system is crucial to our business, the new solution must be operational shortly after an agreement has been reached with the chosen supplier," the bourse said.
